exceptions.justification: Crash reporter manifest tests use an example.invalid upload URL with dummy userinfo to prove the manifest writer strips credentials; the value is a synthetic fixture, not a live endpoint.
Crash reporter manifest tests feed sentinel SMTP passwords (another-secret, smtp-secret-sentinel) to prove they are never persisted; synthetic fixtures only.
Engine settings tests parse an UploadURL with dummy userinfo on crash.example.invalid to prove settings redaction; synthetic fixture only.
OPS-100 redaction tests plant a credential-bearing URL to prove the redactor removes it; the fixture is synthetic and asserted redacted.
OPS-100 adversarial tests plant PEM private-key headers with fake bodies to prove the bounded PEM parser redacts matched, mismatched and unterminated blocks; no real key material.
OPS-100 redaction tests plant a PEM private-key header with a fake body to prove it is redacted; no real key material.
Signing tests protect a throwaway self-signed PFX generated inside the test with the literal password testpass; it never guards a real certificate.
DATA-120 persistence tests write account rows with placeholder salt and passwordHash values (s, h) to exercise schema migration; not credentials.
DATA-120 secrets-at-rest tests plant named canary passwords (Od22-*-Canary) and hunter2 to prove OD-22 plaintext secrets never reach disk; synthetic canaries.
SEC-100 dedicated-server tests use SEC100_FAKE_* sentinel strings to prove RCON arguments and responses are not logged; synthetic sentinels.
MMO credential tests use the literal owned-string-secret to prove sensitive buffers are wiped; synthetic fixture.
Remote debug tests use a sentinel payload string to prove sensitive payloads never enter the audit log; synthetic sentinel.
Console concurrency tests use a sentinel credential string to prove it never persists to history; synthetic sentinel.
TF-120 save-root tests write account rows with placeholder salt and passwordHash values to exercise shared-save migration; not credentials.
TF onboarding tests build account JSON with placeholder passwordHash values (hash) to exercise schema validation; not credentials.
OPS-100 adversarial tests plant structured password, api_key and connection_string assignments to prove the lexer redacts them; synthetic fixtures.
OPS-100 crash-security tests plant a password field in a crash payload to prove the package validator rejects it; synthetic fixture.
OPS-100 redaction tests plant structured credentials across key spellings to prove redaction; synthetic fixtures.
OPS-100 telemetry spool tests plant a password field in a spool record to prove the spool validator rejects it; synthetic fixture.
Site-data contract test asserts that the removed rconPassword admin123 example no longer appears in the quick-start docs; the literal is the forbidden text itself.

The self-signed signing precursor prints the names of the GitHub environment secrets an operator must provision (SPARK_RELEASE_SIGNING_PFX_BASE64 and SPARK_RELEASE_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD) after an 'Environment secret:' label; the right-hand side is a variable name, never a value.
